search_log: Searched "Shopgirl Steve Martin excerpt first chapter publisher" and reviewed the Hachette publisher listing; it verified the work but supplied no usable prose excerpt.

Searched "Shopgirl Steve Martin third person narrator point of view" and "Shopgirl Steve Martin omniscient narrator analysis"; opened the BlackFilm author interview, eNotes analysis, and A.V. Club review.

Searched Google Books and Internet Archive for an authorized or library-hosted excerpt; Google Books exposed only catalog/limited-preview metadata and could not be opened for usable prose, while no relevant Internet Archive text was found.
Found a sustained chapter transcription on ESL-Bits but did not rely on it because its authorization and provenance were unclear.
Searched the isolated line "So, I can hurt now, or hurt later"; results attributed it to Mirabelle, confirming that its first person is local character speech or thought rather than a narrator shift.
Follow-up searches found Publishers Weekly's explicit comparison describing Shopgirl's narration as distanced and omniscient; no credible evidence of alternating or participating narration was found.
person_note: The quotes repeatedly show an external narrator moving among Mirabelle's, Ray's, and Jeremy's thoughts and correcting characters' incomplete perceptions. Steve Martin's own interview explicitly calls the book's narrator omniscient, and several independent reviews agree. The lone first-person quote belongs locally to Mirabelle, while generic uses of 'you' are aphoristic rather than second-person storytelling. The controlling base narration is therefore third-person omniscient; the lack of an opened authorized full excerpt is offset by extensive quote evidence and strong explicit whole-book web evidence.
